Portugal wedding venues run from Sintra palaces to Algarve cliffs.
Foreign couples start the legal process for a wedding in Portugal at least one month before the date.
Some couples hold a symbolic ceremony in Portugal and marry legally at home.

sections.body_md:
## Fall for Portugal Before You Choose a Venue

Before you compare venues, see what Portugal offers: romantic palaces in the Sintra hills that can be booked for a wedding, and the terraced vineyards of the Alto Douro Wine Region for your guests.

### Pena, Sintra
The legacy of Ferdinand II, the King-Artist: a coloured, castle-like palace crowning the Sintra hills in a wooded park.

### Monserrate, Sintra
A Romantic estate created by 19th-century collector Francis Cook, with exotic gardens and a palace by James Knowles Jr. It hosts private celebrations.

### Queluz, Near Lisbon
A national palace near Lisbon. Parques de Sintra offers its upper gardens and Throne Room for celebrations.

### The Douro Valley
The Alto Douro Wine Region, UNESCO World Heritage since 2001: about 2,000 years of winemaking, steep terraced vineyards and wine quintas.

[APPLY AFTER SIGN-OFF: F076, Project Lead (human)] ### Ponta da Piedade, Algarve
Golden sea stacks and grottoes on the western Algarve, near Lagos, for clifftop photographs the day after the wedding.
[FALLBACK UNTIL THEN] ### The Algarve Coast
Clifftop and beach settings on Portugal's southern coast.

For the customs behind the day, read about [Portuguese wedding traditions](/7-ancient-and-romantic-portuguese-wedding-traditions), from azulejo tiles to fado, the Lisbon song UNESCO lists as intangible heritage.

## Choose Your Region of Portugal

We group Portugal wedding venues into five regions, each with its own setting, served by four airports. Pick the one that fits, whether you are planning an elopement, a small wedding or a three-day weekend. Not sure which region? Your Wedded Advisor helps you choose.

### Lisbon, Sintra and Cascais
- Setting: Sintra's palaces, Lisbon and the Cascais coast
- Nearest airport: Lisbon (LIS)

Lisbon wedding venues include a public municipal space for civil ceremonies at Lisbon City Council.

[Button: Ask about Lisbon and Sintra](#enquire) (prefills Region: Lisbon, Sintra and Cascais)

CMS note: the palace rules strip (add-palace-rules) sits here, under this card.

### The Algarve
- Setting: Algarve wedding venues on clifftops and beaches
- Nearest airport: Faro (FAO)

Beach weddings need a permit: from the local council on designated bathing beaches, or from the Captain of the Port elsewhere on the coast.

[Button: Ask about the Algarve](#enquire) (prefills Region: The Algarve)

- Setting: wine quintas in the Alto Douro Wine Region
- Nearest airport: Porto (OPO)

Among the [Europe wedding destinations](/destinations/europe) on Wedded Wonderland, a destination wedding in Portugal gives couples five things in one country.

sections.body_md:
## Pick the Setting for Your Ceremony

We sort Portugal wedding venues into six settings.

**Quinta.** A Portuguese country or wine estate. Some have rooms, so guests can stay where you marry; [see what to check](#venue-charges) before you book exclusive use.

**Palace or pousada.** Sintra's palaces are booked through Parques de Sintra, and Pousadas de Portugal hosts weddings in historic palaces, castles and monasteries.

**Clifftop or beach.** Atlantic views on the Algarve and the west coast.

**Vineyard estate.** Terraced vineyards and wine quintas in the Alto Douro Wine Region.

**In the city.** Lisbon City Council and Albufeira City Council offer public municipal spaces for civil ceremonies.

**Catholic church or another faith.** Catholic marriage is one of three recognised forms and is still registered through the civil registry. Other faiths can use civil marriage in religious form.

Portuguese venues price in different ways, so we check four things with you before you sign.

## Plan Your Portugal Wedding, Step by Step

Legal and travel details checked October 2026, with official sources named.

Tabs (all panels in the DOM, not loaded on click): Getting there | Entry rules | Marrying legally | Costs | Your weekend

### Getting There
(Tab label: Getting there)

Four airports serve the five regions on this page.

- **Lisbon (LIS):** Lisbon, Sintra and Cascais; Comporta and the Alentejo
- **Porto (OPO):** Porto and the Douro Valley
- **Faro (FAO):** the Algarve
- **Madeira (FNC), Funchal:** Madeira

Many Lisbon-area venues are 15 to 30 minutes from the city centre, as a guide; we confirm the transfer time for each venue.

### Entry Rules by Passport
(Tab label: Entry rules; anchor: #entry-rules)

**US passport.** No visa is needed for stays of 90 days or less. Your passport needs 3 months' validity beyond your departure date and 2 blank pages. Source: [US Department of State](https://travel.state.gov/content/travel/en/international-travel/International-Travel-Country-Information-Pages/Portugal.html).

**UK passport.** Travel to the Schengen area without a visa for up to 90 days in any 180-day period. Your passport must be issued less than 10 years before you arrive and expire at least 3 months after you leave. EES may record fingerprints and a photo. Source: [GOV.UK entry requirements](https://www.gov.uk/foreign-travel-advice/portugal/entry-requirements).

**Australian passport.** Visit the Schengen area, which includes Portugal, without a visa for up to 90 days in any 180-day period. Under the Entry/Exit System (EES), fingerprints and a photo are taken on arrival at no cost. ETIAS has no confirmed start date. Source: [Smartraveller Portugal advice](https://www.smartraveller.gov.au/destinations/europe/portugal).

### Marrying Legally, by Passport
(Tab label: Marrying legally; anchor: #marrying-legally)

Portugal's civil registry rules apply to every couple, whatever your passport. We walk you through the exact route for your nationality.

1. **Contact the Registo Civil.** Start the marriage process online or in person at any Registo Civil (Portugal's civil registry office).
2. **Gather your documents.** ID, a birth certificate, and a certificate of capacity to marry from the last six months, or a statement that your country issues none.
3. **Submit at least one month before your date.** The registrar agrees the date, time and place; a ceremony away from the registry or out of hours is agreed in advance.
4. **Marry within six months of approval.** The registrar's authorisation gives you up to six months. Your marriage is valid only once it is registered.

Good to know:
- Documents in English, French or Spanish need no translation; others need a certified translation into Portuguese.
- If you do not speak Portuguese and the official does not speak your language, an interpreter is appointed.
- Witnesses are optional: two to four may take part.
- Both partners must be 18 or over.
- You declare one of three forms: civil, Catholic, or civil marriage in religious form.
- [APPLY AFTER SIGN-OFF: F024, Nic] The civil registry fee is EUR 120 at the registry, or EUR 200 outside the registry, out of hours, at weekends or on public holidays.
[FALLBACK UNTIL THEN] The civil registry charges a fee for the ceremony.

#### US Passport
The US Embassy in Lisbon does not issue a CNI, because no US authority exists to issue one.
[APPLY AFTER SIGN-OFF: F043, Nic] The Embassy says you sign a statement of eligibility to marry before a consular officer instead, at a notarial appointment costing USD 50, or the euro equivalent, per notarisation.
[FALLBACK UNTIL THEN] Check the US Embassy's marriage page for the document Portugal accepts.
The Embassy advises allowing at least four weeks for processing. These steps apply to US citizens only.

#### UK Passport
If you live in Portugal or another country outside the UK, you do not need a CNI to marry in Portugal. If the registrar asks for one, show the British Embassy's notice on marriage in Portugal. If you live in the UK, use the FCDO online service to see which document you might need; you need a valid British passport to use it.

#### Australian Passport
To prove you are free to marry, the usual documents are a Certificate of No Impediment to Marriage (CNI) or certificates from a registry of births, deaths and marriages. The Australian Embassy in Lisbon can issue a CNI. DFAT also issues CNIs in Australia, but some countries accept only a CNI issued locally. Confirm with the Registo Civil or the Embassy of Portugal in Canberra which document you need and where it must be issued. An overseas marriage cannot be registered in Australia, but in most cases it is legally recognised if it was valid in Portugal and would be valid under Australian law.

Sources: [Justiça](https://justica.gov.pt/Registos/Civil/Casamento) and [IRN](https://irn.justica.gov.pt/Servicos/Cidadao/Casamento/Organizar-o-casamento); the [US Embassy in Lisbon](https://pt.usembassy.gov/marriage-in-portugal/); GOV.UK on [living in Portugal](https://www.gov.uk/guidance/living-in-portugal) and the [FCDO service](https://www.gov.uk/marriages-civil-partnerships-abroad/get-documents-for-a-marriage-or-civil-partnership-abroad); [Smartraveller on marrying overseas](https://www.smartraveller.gov.au/planning-trip/advice-your-planned-activities/getting-married-overseas) and the [Australian Embassy in Lisbon](https://portugal.embassy.gov.au/lbon/marriage.html).

## Get Answers Before You Enquire

### 1. What Are the Requirements for Getting Married in Portugal?
Foreign couples marry through Portugal's civil registry: start the process online or at any Registo Civil at least one month before your date, and marry within six months of approval. You need ID, a birth certificate and a certificate of capacity to marry from the last six months, or a statement that your country issues none. The full steps by passport are under [Marrying legally](#marrying-legally).

### 2. Can US, UK or Australian Citizens Get Legally Married in Portugal?
Yes, but each passport proves freedom to marry in a different way. US citizens: the US Embassy in Lisbon does not issue a CNI (Certificate of No Impediment).
[APPLY AFTER SIGN-OFF: F043, Nic] The Embassy says you sign a statement of eligibility before a consular officer instead.
[FALLBACK UNTIL THEN] Check the US Embassy's marriage page for the document Portugal accepts.
UK nationals living outside the UK need no CNI; UK residents check the FCDO online service. Australians: the Australian Embassy in Lisbon can issue a CNI; confirm with the Registo Civil or the Embassy of Portugal in Canberra which document you need.

### 3. Is a Catholic or Symbolic Ceremony Legal in Portugal?
Yes for a Catholic ceremony: Catholic marriage is one of three legally recognised forms in Portugal, and it is valid once registered with the civil registry. A symbolic ceremony is not a legal marriage by itself. Other faiths can marry through civil marriage in religious form, with a church or religious community established in Portugal.

### 4. How Much Is an Average Wedding in Portugal?
[APPLY AFTER SIGN-OFF: F069, Nic] EUR 25,000 to 70,000 for about 100 guests, according to Rita Plácido Photography (listed October 2026). Catering runs EUR 80 to 200 per person including drinks, and venue rental about EUR 3,000 to 15,000 or more. These are third-party figures, not Wedded Wonderland prices, and amounts in AUD, USD or GBP vary with the exchange rate.
[FALLBACK UNTIL THEN] There is no single average: the cost depends on your guest count, the region, the season, the nights you take the venue and whether you book it for exclusive use. Wedded Concierge talks you through the options for your plans.

### 5. When Can You Get Married in Portugal?
On a date you agree with the registrar, at least one month after you organise the civil process and within six months of approval. For weather, travel guides often recommend spring or autumn. Heat waves are common in July and August, wildfire risk is highest from June to September, and heavy rain is most common from October to February.

### 6. Where Is the Best Place to Get Married in Portugal?
Portugal has five wedding regions, served by four airports: Lisbon, Sintra and Cascais; the Algarve; Porto and the Douro Valley; Comporta and the Alentejo; and Madeira. Choose Sintra for palaces, the Algarve for clifftops and beaches, the Douro for vineyards, Comporta for the Alentejo coast and Madeira for an Atlantic island. Fly into Lisbon (LIS), Faro (FAO), Porto (OPO) or Madeira (FNC).

### 7. What Are Some Good Wedding Venues in the Algarve, Portugal?
Algarve wedding venues include clifftop and beach settings, and Albufeira City Council offers a public municipal space for civil ceremonies. Ask us which suit your guest count.

### 8. Can You Have a Beach Wedding in Portugal?
Yes, a beach wedding in Portugal is possible with a permit. On designated bathing beaches, the local council licenses events under Decree-Law 97/2018; elsewhere on the coast, the local Captain of the Port is responsible. Ask us which applies to the beach you have in mind.

### 9. Can You Have a Small Wedding or Elopement in Portugal?
Yes. Witnesses are optional in a Portuguese civil ceremony, so the two of you can marry with no guests at all, once the civil process has started at least one month ahead.
[APPLY AFTER SIGN-OFF: F024, Nic] A civil ceremony at the registry costs EUR 120, or EUR 200 outside the registry or out of hours.
[FALLBACK UNTIL THEN] The simplest route is a civil ceremony at the registry, for a fee.
Or hold a symbolic ceremony in Portugal and marry legally at home, as some couples do.

### 10. Can You Get Married in a Sintra Palace?
Yes: Parques de Sintra hires out Monserrate, Pena, Queluz, the National Palace of Sintra and the Portuguese School of Equestrian Art for private celebrations, including weddings. State events can cancel bookings at Queluz or the National Palace of Sintra, and Monserrate's roof works run until the first quarter of 2027.

faq.q: Can US, UK or Australian Citizens Get Legally Married in Portugal?
faq.a:
Yes, but each passport proves freedom to marry in a different way. US citizens: the US Embassy in Lisbon does not issue a CNI (Certificate of No Impediment).
[APPLY AFTER SIGN-OFF: F043, Nic] The Embassy says you sign a statement of eligibility before a consular officer instead.
[FALLBACK UNTIL THEN] Check the US Embassy's marriage page for the document Portugal accepts.
UK nationals living outside the UK need no CNI; UK residents check the FCDO online service. Australians: the Australian Embassy in Lisbon can issue a CNI; confirm with the Registo Civil or the Embassy of Portugal in Canberra which document you need and where it must be issued.

faq.q: Is a Catholic or Symbolic Ceremony Legal in Portugal?
faq.a: Yes for a Catholic ceremony: Catholic marriage is one of three legally recognised forms in Portugal, and it is valid once registered with the civil registry. A symbolic ceremony is not a legal marriage by itself. Other faiths can marry through civil marriage in religious form, with a church or religious community established in Portugal.

faq.q: How Much Is an Average Wedding in Portugal?
faq.a:
[APPLY AFTER SIGN-OFF: F069, Nic] EUR 25,000 to 70,000 for about 100 guests, according to Rita Plácido Photography (listed October 2026). Catering runs EUR 80 to 200 per person including drinks, and venue rental about EUR 3,000 to 15,000 or more. These are third-party figures, not Wedded Wonderland prices, and amounts in AUD, USD or GBP vary with the exchange rate.
[FALLBACK UNTIL THEN] There is no single average: the cost depends on your guest count, the region, the season, the nights you take the venue and whether you book it for exclusive use. Wedded Concierge talks you through the options for your plans.

faq.q: When Can You Get Married in Portugal?
faq.a: On a date you agree with the registrar, at least one month after you organise the civil process and within six months of approval. For weather, travel guides often recommend spring or autumn. Heat waves are common in July and August, wildfire risk is highest from June to September, and heavy rain is most common from October to February.

faq.q: Where Is the Best Place to Get Married in Portugal?
faq.a: Portugal has five wedding regions, served by four airports: Lisbon, Sintra and Cascais; the Algarve; Porto and the Douro Valley; Comporta and the Alentejo; and Madeira. Choose Sintra for palaces, the Algarve for clifftops and beaches, the Douro for vineyards, Comporta for the Alentejo coast and Madeira for an Atlantic island. Fly into Lisbon (LIS), Faro (FAO), Porto (OPO) or Madeira (FNC).

faq.q: What Are Some Good Wedding Venues in the Algarve, Portugal?
faq.a: Algarve wedding venues include clifftop and beach settings, and Albufeira City Council offers a public municipal space for civil ceremonies. Ask us which suit your guest count.

faq.q: Can You Have a Beach Wedding in Portugal?
faq.a: Yes, a beach wedding in Portugal is possible with a permit. On designated bathing beaches, the local council licenses events under Decree-Law 97/2018; elsewhere on the coast, the local Captain of the Port is responsible. Ask us which applies to the beach you have in mind.

faq.q: Can You Have a Small Wedding or Elopement in Portugal?
faq.a:
Yes. Witnesses are optional in a Portuguese civil ceremony, so the two of you can marry with no guests at all, once the civil process has started at least one month ahead.
[APPLY AFTER SIGN-OFF: F024, Nic] A civil ceremony at the registry costs EUR 120, or EUR 200 outside the registry or out of hours.
[FALLBACK UNTIL THEN] The simplest route is a civil ceremony at the registry, for a fee.
Or hold a symbolic ceremony in Portugal and marry legally at home, as some couples do.

faq.q: Can You Get Married in a Sintra Palace?
faq.a: Yes: Parques de Sintra hires out Monserrate, Pena, Queluz, the National Palace of Sintra and the Portuguese School of Equestrian Art for private celebrations, including weddings. State events can cancel bookings at Queluz or the National Palace of Sintra, and Monserrate's roof works run until the first quarter of 2027.
